content: In accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines for the declaration of interests by experts, all members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), External Review Group (ERG), and evidence reviewers were required to complete WHO Declaration of Interest (DOI) forms. They were also mandated to disclose in writing any competing interests—whether academic, financial, or otherwise—that could potentially conflict with their roles in the development of the guidelines. To ensure neutrality and independence, the WHO Guideline Steering Committee conducted a thorough assessment of the DOI forms, curricula vitae, research interests, and professional activities of the experts. In cases where potential conflicts of interest were identified, the WHO Office for Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics was consulted for further clarification and advice on managing these conflicts. If any declared interests were deemed significant, the individuals were excluded from serving as members of the GDG. A public notice was issued to allow the public to provide comments on any competing interests that may have been overlooked or unreported during the initial assessments. Members Declaring No Conflicts of Interest The following GDG members declared no conflicts of interest: Holger Schünemann (Chair) Rafael Laniado-Laborin (Co-Chair) Erlina Burhan Fernanda Dockhorn Costa Johansen Bernard Fourie Elmira Gurbanova Muhammad Amir Khan Marian Loveday Mahshid Nasehi Ben Marais Beatrice Mutayoba Maria Rodríguez Debrah Vambe Nguyen Viet Nhung One member, Ingrid Schoeman, provided additional information but required no further action as it did not result in any conflict. As a survivor of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB), she experienced the side effects of a two-year treatment regimen. She has been employed by TB Proof, an advocacy organization, since 2017. Her work involves sharing the experiences of drug-resistant TB survivors and advocating for high-quality TB care. She believes that evidence-based guidelines for treating drug-resistant TB would benefit her colleagues, friends, and local communities. Members Declaring Non-Significant Interests Six GDG members declared interests that were judged non-significant and not affecting their independence or impartiality during the guideline development process. Therefore, no restrictions were applied to their participation: Charles Daley: Participated in the Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) for delamanid trials, receiving $5,000 in 2016 and $4,000 for ongoing services. These payments were made by Otsuka Pharmaceutical. Gerry Davies: Engaged in the PreDICT-TB consortium, a public-private partnership funded by the European Union. His role as academic coordinator (2012–2017) involved collaboration with industrial partners in pre-competitive TB drug research. He also collaborates on pharmacokinetic sub-studies related to the STREAM Stage 1 trial and the TB-PRACTECAL trial. Funding for these activities was provided through public institutions, with no direct financial support from pharmaceutical companies. Yuhong Liu: Supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and Janssen Pharmaceutica for China’s New Drug Introduction and Protection Program (NDIP). This included a $500,000 grant for project implementation between 2016 and 2020. No financial interests were identified that could compromise professional judgment. Iqbal Master: Received non-monetary support from Janssen Pharmaceutica to attend the 2016 International Lung Conference. His involvement in research studies, including STREAM 1 and the Nix-TB trial, was purely altruistic, with no monetary compensation. Payam Nahid: Participated in clinical trial units supported by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and served on the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) for the TB-PRACTECAL trial. Discussions with Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) for future collaborations are ongoing, with no formal agreements in place. Carrie Tudor: Managed a TB project funded by the Eli Lilly Foundation through the International Council of Nurses, receiving approximately $1,000,000 between 2013 and 2019. Members Declaring Significant Interests The following GDG members declared significant interests that required further discussion and management plans by the WHO Office for Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics: Susan Abdel-Rahman: Received $197,000 in research support from the Thrasher Foundation for pediatric medical research. This funding ended in 2017. No financial interests were identified that could compromise her professional judgment. Daniela Cirillo: Received research grants totaling $80,000 in 2018 to study minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) for new TB drugs. These grants were provided through Ospedale San Raffaele by Janssen Therapeutics and the TB Alliance. Payments were made to the institution, not directly to the individual. Kelly Dooley: Served as Principal Investigator (PI) for the APT trial assessing pretomanid for drug-sensitive TB. She also participated in multiple NIH-funded studies on TB treatment, with drug donations from pharmaceutical companies. Her involvement in the DELIBERATE study led to partial exclusion from discussions and voting on the combined use of bedaquiline and delamanid. Agnes Gebhard: Received a $305,000 research grant from the TB Alliance to conduct situational analyses and develop roadmaps for introducing new TB regimens in selected countries. This led to partial exclusion from decision-making related to the BPaL regimen. Alberto Piubello: Participated in the STREAM Stage 2 trial, sponsored by The Union, leading to partial exclusion from decision-making on bedaquiline-containing regimens. Alena Skrahina: Principal Investigator for the TB-PRACTECAL trial, leading to partial exclusion from decision-making on the BPaL regimen. Andrew Vernon: Collaborated with NIH and Sanofi on a multinational phase 3 trial of TB treatment using rifapentine. Sanofi provided medications and supported pharmacokinetic testing costs. His involvement led to partial exclusion from decision-making on the BPaL regimen. External Review Group (ERG) The following ERG members declared no conflicts of interest: Heather Alexander Sarabjit Singh Chadha Lisa Chen Edwin H. Herrera-Flores Anna Marie Celina Garfin Mathilde Jachym Giovanni Battista Migliori Thato Mosidi Welile Sikhondze Bhabana Shrestha Ivan Solovic Carlos Torres Zarir Udwadia One ERG member, Amanullah Farhana, declared employment and consultancy work for WHO and research activities funded by WHO and the Global Fund. Another member, Guy Marks, declared his role as President of The Union (IUATLD) and investigator on the VQUIN trial, a publicly funded study on preventive therapy for MDR-TB contacts. Neither declaration was judged to conflict with the objectives of the guidelines. This version maintains the detailed information while presenting it in a clear, professional, and structured manner.
